entries.intent: Single preserved selected subject delivered post-detach; launcher-preopened read-only compatibility path bound to preserved capture digest
Single declared disposable sanitized derivative sink slot; launcher-precreated empty regular file handed over O_APPEND and broker-collected after worker exit

notes: This later-worker map stays tiny and does not grant any authoritative-store directory preopen.
The worker-visible input path is compatibility-only plumbing; the launcher-preopened preserved-subject file remains the input authority anchor.
Receipt-visible derivative egress leaves only through one declared launcher-precreated disposable sink file; worker outbox paths are not authoritative derivative identity.
Path re-open, store rebinding, and authoritative-store write/browse authority stay out in this first removable-media local fallback lane.
The first lane admits exactly one declared writable derivative sink slot and no extra writable result surface.
Receipt-visible derivative egress leaves only through launcher-precreated disposable sink files; worker outbox paths are not authoritative derivative identity.
The one declared writable sink slot starts as a launcher-precreated empty regular file and is handed to the worker already opened O_APPEND.

The later worker gets no CAP_READ, CAP_FTRUNCATE, or CAP_FCNTL on that slot; CAP_SEEK appears only as seekable-file ballast, the sink stays append-only-protected while the worker runs, and derivative egress stays append-open with no worker readback or truncate.
The launcher or its approved shim enters capability mode before handing control to later tool mainline code.
After cap_enter no ambient absolute-path opens remain; any later path-compatible behavior must already be satisfied by the preopened capability set.
If a tool cannot run on that preopened capability set after cap_enter, it stays out of this first removable-media local fallback lane unless a later explicit wrapper/broker contract earns it.
The reviewed later-worker descriptor set stays closed-world; the launcher closes or spawn-closefroms every non-reviewed descriptor before handing control to later tool code.

stdin stays inert null/empty input only; stdout/stderr stay launcher-owned observation channels or reviewed append-only log sinks, and no parent TTY/session socket is inherited into this first removable-media local fallback lane.
The later worker environment posture is reviewed-minimal-env-no-inherited-parent-env; the launcher constructs the reviewed allowlist and does not inherit the parent environment wholesale.
The later worker argv posture is launcher-reviewed-argv-no-media-derived-args; preserved subject identity arrives through reviewed descriptors rather than media-derived filename arguments.
The later worker cwd posture is launcher-owned-empty-workdir-no-ingest-store-cwd; cwd is launcher-owned scratch at /work, not /ingest, the authoritative store, or parent cwd.

The later worker executable posture is launcher-resolved-executable-digest-no-path-search; the launcher resolves the executable before handoff and no PATH/cwd/media-derived executable lookup occurs in the worker.

Executable digest sha256:abababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababab and wrapper contract digest sha256:bcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbcbc are recorded so support can identify the exact code and launch wrapper that processed the preserved subject.
Helper/plugin discovery posture is no-implicit-helper-or-plugin-discovery; tools that need implicit helpers stay out of this first lane until an explicit wrapper/broker contract admits them.

The later worker runtime dependency posture is launcher-pinned-runtime-dependency-closure-no-ambient-loader-search; runtime libraries/interpreters/helpers are selected from the launcher-pinned closure sha256:cdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcdcd, not from LD_LIBRARY_PATH, cwd, /ingest, media-derived paths, or host-global loader hints.

Dynamic loader posture is no-ld-library-path-cwd-or-media-derived-loader-inputs; late dlopen/helper/plugin/runtime discovery remains out of this first lane unless a later explicit wrapper/broker contract admits and receipts it.

The later worker credential posture is launcher-fixed-unprivileged-credential-envelope-no-supplementary-groups; the launcher fixes the worker user/group to derive-rm-worker:derive-rm-worker before tool mainline and no parent/root credential is inherited.
Supplementary groups posture is no-supplementary-groups; the worker receives an empty supplementary group vector, not the launcher's login/session groups.
Privilege regain posture is no-setuid-setgid-saved-id-or-ambient-privilege-regain; setuid/setgid binaries, saved-id regain, and ambient privilege regain stay out of this first lane.

The later worker process lifecycle posture is launcher-supervised-no-daemon-or-orphan-descendants; the launcher supervises the worker process tree and no daemon/orphan continuation is part of the first lane.

Descendant posture is no-background-descendants-or-unreviewed-subprocesses; helper processes, background subprocesses, daemonization, double-fork, and process-group/session detachment stay out unless a later wrapper/broker contract admits them.
Reap posture is launcher-reaps-entire-worker-tree-before-receipt; the launcher observes worker exit and reaps the entire reviewed worker tree before any derivative receipt becomes authoritative.

The later worker resource envelope posture is launcher-enforced-resource-envelope-no-unbounded-worker-consumption; CPU time, wall clock, memory, open files, process count, scratch bytes, and declared derivative-output bytes are fixed by the launcher before tool mainline starts.

Resource receipt posture is receipt-records-resource-envelope-and-observed-usage; the receipt records both the reviewed limits and observed usage so support does not reconstruct resource authority from host-local logs.

Resource failure posture is resource-limit-hit-fails-closed-no-derivative-authority; if the envelope is exceeded, the lane fails closed and no authoritative derivative locator is minted from partial output.
Output bound posture is declared-derivative-output-size-bound-before-receipt; the single declared sink cannot grow into an unbounded result surface before broker collection and receipt authority.

Peer interaction posture is launcher-isolated-peer-envelope-no-ambient-ptrace-signal-or-ipc; the later worker is isolated from same-UID peers, parent sessions, operator shells, and unrelated worker instances.
Peer-interaction receipt posture is receipt-records-peer-isolation-and-signal-policy; receipts record the peer/signal posture rather than relying on jail or service defaults.
Signal posture is launcher-only-signal-control-no-peer-or-session-control; only the launcher/broker control path may terminate or observe the worker lifecycle.
IPC posture is no-unreviewed-ipc-sockets-shm-pipes-or-procfs; no unreviewed Unix sockets, network sockets, shared memory, pipes, or procfs handles are part of this first lane.
Procfs posture is procfs-ptrace-and-ktrace-unavailable-to-worker-and-peers; ptrace, ktrace, and procfs visibility are unavailable to the worker and ambient peers for this lane.

Network posture is network-egress-absent-no-socket-dns-or-remote-callbacks; the post-detach later worker receives no network socket authority and cannot use DNS, NSS, resolver state, or remote callbacks as derivative input authority.

Network receipt posture is receipt-records-network-absent-envelope; receipts record that the no-network envelope, name-resolution posture, proxy posture, and remote-dependency posture were enforced instead of relying on jail defaults.

Name-resolution posture is no-dns-mdns-nss-or-resolver-host-input; DNS, mDNS, NSS, /etc/hosts, resolver configuration, and directory-backed name service stay out of this first lane unless a later compatibility lane declares and receipts them.
Proxy posture is no-proxy-or-remote-service-configuration; HTTP(S)_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, NO_PROXY, PAC files, and desktop proxy settings are not admitted into the post-detach worker.

Remote-dependency posture is no-remote-fetch-or-callback-derivative-authority; remote fetch, license checks, telemetry, safe-browsing lookups, update pings, and callback/reporting channels cannot shape ordinary derivative output.

Persistent state posture is persistent-state-absent-no-home-cache-or-host-state-writes; the later worker receives no user-home, host-cache, host-config, history, crash-dump, durable tool-state, or reusable temporary-state authority.

Persistent-state receipt posture is receipt-records-persistent-state-absence-and-scratch-cleanup; the receipt records durable-state absence and scratch cleanup instead of relying on disposable-jail folklore.
Scratch posture is launcher-created-empty-scratch-nonauthoritative; any scratch is launcher-created, initially empty, per-run, bounded by the resource envelope, and nonauthoritative.
Scratch cleanup posture is scratch-destroyed-before-derivative-receipt; scratch cleanup must complete before derivative receipt authority is minted.

Cache/config posture is no-user-home-cache-config-or-history-state; XDG home/cache/config/state, tool history, thumbnail/font/plugin caches, crash dumps, and reusable TMPDIR state stay out of this first lane.
The post-detach contract closure is schema-backed and guarded by positive plus negative fixtures; receipts must bind backend launch evidence rather than relying on posture prose alone.
r511 fresh-authority receipt keeps post-tombstone successor access on a fresh lease, new digest subjects, and a new policy decision instead of stale-handle replay.
